The book's entry for "Garment" narrows the consensus primary meaning to a single, precise identification: the fine linen garment in Revelation 19:8 is explicitly the righteous acts of the saints. This is not a contradiction but a refinement that keeps the central referent (righteousness as divine covering) while tightening the boundary to the deeds-of-the-saints reading of that verse. The consensus already treats that reading as one of two viable options within the same broad category; the book simply selects and foregrounds the deeds interpretation as the entry's core definition. All other consensus alternatives (status, body, mourning, etc.) remain untouched. The 19:8 citation alone supplies strong support for the book's claim, as it is the exact verse the entry quotes. Overall relationship is REFINED.
